name: Eric Slifka
current_role: President, CEO and Chairman of the Board, Global Partners LP (NYSE: GLP); named chairman in 2025 succeeding his uncle Richard Slifka
profile: Eric Slifka runs Global Partners LP, a Massachusetts-based fuel distribution, terminal and convenience-store MLP. He grew up in the family's home heating oil business with his father Fred Slifka, became COO of Global Companies in 1998, President and CEO in 2003, and led the 2005 IPO as an MLP; the company has since grown more than tenfold.
interesting_fact: He led Global Partners' 2005 IPO as a master limited partnership; since then the company has grown more than tenfold and paid more than $1 billion in distributions to unitholders.
deep_cut_fact: He learned the business hands-on from childhood alongside his father at the family's retail home heating oil company, later working terminals, bulk operations, vessel movements and truck loading racks; he sits on the National Petroleum Council and the board of the Energy Policy Research Foundation.
notes: Energy-relevant guest (fuel terminals, energy transition). name: Richard Marko
current_role: CEO, ESET (Bratislava-based cybersecurity company), since January 2011
profile: Slovak computer scientist who joined ESET during his university studies, co-authored the ESET NOD32 antivirus scanning engine, became CTO in 2008 and CEO in 2011. His wealth stems from his stake in ESET. In May 2026 he announced a EUR 40m investment in AI-powered cybersecurity at ESET World 2026 in Berlin, stressing European tech sovereignty.
interesting_fact: Under Marko, ESET said in 2026 it had scanned nearly 800,000 unique AI agent 'skills' since March 2026, flagging ~25,000 as suspicious and blocking 3,000+ as malicious; he argues cybersecurity 'cannot depend entirely on models controlled by Big Tech'.
deep_cut_fact: He began as chief software architect of ESET's scanning core and co-authored the NOD32 engine; per Starmus, in 2002 he developed an AI-based heuristic method that helped counter email-borne virus outbreaks, later extended into malware 'DNA' detection. He also sits on the board of the ESET Foundation (ESET Science Award).
notes: Rebecca Kiely is Director of Global PR and Communication (best global route); pr@eset.com is the North America press team. Repeatedly voted Slovakia's most respected CEO in PwC/Forbes surveys. Regular speaker (Starmus, GLOBSEC). Good AI/sovereignty angle.

name: Zhao Zhiya
current_role: Co-founder of Kuang-Chi (光启); since Nov 2022 responsible for fundamental/frontier research at the controlling-shareholder group level (left listed Kuang-Chi Technologies' board and GM post)
profile: Dr. Zhao Zhiya is one of five founders of Shenzhen-based Kuang-Chi, a metamaterials company whose founding team came out of a Duke University research lab before 2010. He served as president/general manager and director of the listed Kuang-Chi Technologies until November 2022, when he resigned to lead fundamental, frontier research at the controlling-shareholder group.
interesting_fact: In 2020 he said Kuang-Chi aimed to be 'the Qian Xuesen of the new era', projecting about RMB 1bn of metamaterial orders that year and capacity of 48 tons by year-end, insisting the company was 'not drawing pie in the sky'.
deep_cut_fact: Per the company's Nov 2022 SZSE filing, he stepped down as director and GM of Kuang-Chi Technologies not to leave but to take on 'foundational, pioneering research' at the controlling-shareholder group level.
notes: Low public profile since 2022; no personal channels found. Route would be via Kuang-Chi (光启) corporate/IR channels (not verified in this pass). Founding team linked to Duke University metamaterials lab per The Paper.

name: Li Chunrong
